claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
Applying a thin, adherent anti-oxidation coating will significantly improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating can improve oxidation resistance without sacrificing the alloy's intrinsic mechanical performance.
An alumina-based ceramic coating is a candidate anti-oxidation coating for this alloy.
The proposed operating boundary is exposure to air at approximately 1000 °C for approximately 100 hours.
The proposed mechanical-loading boundary is a strain rate of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr.
Restricting oxygen diffusion prevents deep oxidation and maintains the alloy microstructure.
A stable protective coating at high temperature reduces oxygen ingress and reaction with the alloy constituents.
Reducing oxygen ingress prevents formation of detrimental oxide scales that would compromise mechanical properties.
Coated samples will have significantly lower oxide-scale thickness than uncoated samples after the specified exposure.
Coated samples will have lower oxygen uptake than uncoated samples after the specified exposure.
The post-exposure tensile ductility and yield strength of coated samples will remain comparable to those of untreated cast samples.
Uncoated HfNbTaTiZr undergoes extensive oxidation in high-temperature air, leading to mechanical-performance degradation.
Adequate coating adhesion and thermal compatibility with the substrate are necessary for successful protection.
Long-term adhesion and thermal-expansion mismatch may limit coating performance.
